plan.summary: Articles filed under 2+ shows with one shared pull quote (audit-shared-url-quote.js): give each show its own section quote and score, flag misfiled copies, human-clear flags that misread a multi-show column. Part 2 of 6.

actions.oldValue: Both arrive with clarity and purpose, and both serve as reminders of what the Broadway musical, carefully wrought, can accomplish.
actions.newValue: The remarkable thing about Buena Vista Social Club is that it radiates emotional authenticity and political undercurrents without ever tipping into maudlin nostalgia or angry agitprop.
actions.description: joint closing quote replaced with BVSC section quote

actions.oldValue: If the whole isn’t greater than the sum of its parts, Hadestown still has effective elements that come together for the best atmosphere on Broadway.
actions.newValue: That their barriers will break down seems inevitable, but the joy is in Wilson’s colorful and poetic writing, and in this case, the excellent direction and performances.
BRO-4599: Burn This section is a near-rave (praises writing, direction, Driver; minor chemistry reservation). Score from that section only.

actions.oldValue: And this bawdy crowd-pleaser at least has the courage of its crackpot convictions.
actions.newValue: “Cats: The Jellicle Ball" didn’t make me rethink my opinion of the musical, though this hoary cat really might have nine lives.
BRO-4599: Cats section is positive with reservations: exhilarating concept, choreography, costumes and De Shields, but overlong, over-reverent score and murky sound.

actions.oldValue: Trip Cullman oversees a sharp production that will leave you in stitches, anchored by Ehrenreich’s delicious performance as a man unafraid to be insufferable.
actions.newValue: As synth-powered entertainment, it’s exhilarating. As a display of loose-limbed fabulosity, it’s a marvel.
BRO-4599: Cats section is a rave: triumph of reinvention, exhilarating, feels at home on Broadway.

actions.oldValue: Trip Cullman oversees a sharp production that will leave you in stitches, anchored by Ehrenreich’s delicious performance as a man unafraid to be insufferable.
actions.newValue: Eerily atmospheric and impeccably cast, this “Death of a Salesman” finds vitality in the macabre.
BRO-4599: Death of a Salesman section is a rave: seismic revival, inspired Lane casting, Metcalf monologue for the ages.

actions.oldValue: The real reason this production works is the acting, especially the two leads and two actors in smaller roles.
actions.newValue: Hersh Ellis directs this all smoothly, and Stein does a good job making the audience question what we would do if we were ever offered this hypothetical offer.
BRO-4599: Fish in the Dark section is a pan: calls the script dreck and cynical, faults direction and David's humor.

actions.oldValue: If the whole isn’t greater than the sum of its parts, Hadestown still has effective elements that come together for the best atmosphere on Broadway.
actions.newValue: the result might not merit its tonal shifts from lunacy to philosophical ruminations about class struggle to lunacy again, but it’s definitely more giddily elevating than the inevitable Kool and the Gang jukebox show.
BRO-4599: Gary section is mixed-positive: cheers the burlesque and cast but says the absurdism lacks grounding and pitch is hysterical.

actions.oldValue: “A Woman Among Women” is not just an exercise in transposition; it takes on a life of its own.
actions.newValue: The exchange is a clue to the different approach that the stage version takes, simultaneously more authentic and more artful (also less linear.)
actions.description: shared quote came from the A Woman Among Women section
section is appreciative with reservations about the songs

actions.newValue: BRO-4599: Two-show column. Girl, Interrupted section praises ensemble and adaptation but says songs rarely advance the story; mild positive, scored 70 from that section only.

actions.oldValue: For all his rock-star strutting, he shows us the commoner who became a statesman while grappling with personal and national crises.
actions.newValue: Under Matthew Warchus' predictably expert direction, Hyde Pierce is both anchor and graceful second banana to Mark Rylance's babbling, flatulent, uproarious Valere.
actions.description: shared quote came from the Andrew Jackson section
3 out of 4 stars for La Bete

actions.newValue: BRO-4599: Two-show column, La Bete section rated 3/4 stars: expert direction, uproarious Rylance; 74.
